# KlickBox

> Multi-tenant iPhone task manager with a companion capture surface, the
> Idea Bank. Each User deploys their own OpenClaw agent against a shared
> REST API to manage Tasks, Tags, and the Archive, to process the User's
> Ideas into their own workspace, and to deliver spoken Audio Debriefs the
> User listens to on their phone. The same agent delivers **Reads**: HTML or
> PDF documents the User opens and reads in the app, archived to their own
> iCloud Drive.
> This index is for agents. Start with the integration guide.

Base URL: `https://oyarcsgekpltnxjmidqk.functions.supabase.co/api-key-auth`
That form is for raw HTTP only. A client built from tools.json must be given
the bare host (no `/api-key-auth` — the contract's `base_path` adds it); the
doubled path fails every call with `403 path_not_allowed`, which looks like a
broken deployment and is not.
Auth: send `Authorization: Bearer $KLICKBOX_API_KEY` on every request. The
host is the same for every User; per-User isolation comes from the key.

## Fast path for agents

For **Tasks and Tags**, the tool contract plus the create example below are
enough on their own — fetch https://soltaniehha.com/klickbox-docs/tools.json
and go.

For the **Idea Bank**, read section 6 of the integration guide first. It is
not optional color: it is the only place the content-loss rules are written
out with their failure modes, and every one of those failures is silent — the
call succeeds, the app shows the Idea handled, and the User's words are gone
or stuck. Skipping it is the single most likely way to build an agent that
quietly loses the material it was deployed to look after.

Reach for the domain glossary (context.md) to settle a vocabulary dispute:
what exactly a "Primary Tag", "Effective Score", "Base Score", "Primary
Project", or an "Open" vs "Processed" Idea means.

## Create a Task (works after this single fetch)

```bash
curl -sS \
  "https://oyarcsgekpltnxjmidqk.functions.supabase.co/api-key-auth/rpc/create_task_with_tags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KLICKBOX_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"p_title":"Review the Q2 deck","p_base_score":80,"p_due_date":"2026-05-10T17:00:00Z"}'
# -> { "id": "<task-uuid>", ... }
```

`p_base_score` is 0–100 and **relative to the User's other Tasks**, so GET
the existing tasks first to calibrate (`/tasks?status=eq.active`) rather than
inventing your own scale. See "Choosing a Base Score" in the integration guide.

## Process the Idea Bank (the other loop)

Separate from Tasks, KlickBox holds the User's **Ideas**: captured notes,
quotes, links, screenshots, PDFs, and voice memos, grouped into **Projects**.
An Idea is Open while `needs_processing` is true, a value the server derives
from `processed_at is null or content_updated_at > processed_at`, so there is
no status flag to maintain.

```bash
curl -sS \
  "https://oyarcsgekpltnxjmidqk.functions.supabase.co/api-key-auth/ideas?needs_processing=eq.true&select=*,idea_projects(position,project:projects(*))" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KLICKBOX_API_KEY"
```

Read each Idea's thread, file it into your own per-Project folders, then call
`mark_idea_processed` with the `content_updated_at` you fetched.

Every way this loop loses the User's words is silent: the call succeeds, the
app shows the Idea handled, and the content is gone or stuck Open forever.
Read "Processing the Idea Bank" in the integration guide **before** you write
the loop. The summary below is not a substitute for it.

1. **Echo `content_updated_at` back as the exact string you received.** Never
   `now()`, and never a value you parsed into a date and re-serialized — the
   column has microsecond precision, most date libraries re-serialize at
   milliseconds, and the truncated marker is accepted with no error and leaves
   the Idea reprocessed forever.
2. **Reconcile the whole Idea, not just its Entries.** An Idea reopens for
   **five** reasons: an Entry added, edited or deleted, the **title** edited,
   or an **Attachment** added, removed, or finishing its upload. The last two
   move no Entry at all, so an Entry-only diff reports "nothing changed" on an
   Idea that reopened and you re-mark it, never reading the photo. Snapshot the
   title, each Entry's `(id, updated_at)`, and each Attachment's `(id, status)`.
   If a diff finds no difference at all, stop and do not mark.
3. **Page the results, and never with a growing offset.** Marking removes rows
   from `needs_processing=eq.true`, so offsets computed against the old set
   address the wrong rows in the new one and silently skip a third of a
   backlog. Re-request the first page each time, or keyset-paginate.
4. **Nothing on the server checks that you read anything.** A marker equal to
   the current `content_updated_at` is always accepted. The marker is the only
   record that the work happened.

The guide also covers the per-media rules, attachment `status` (a row can exist
before its blob does), detecting a Reopen, and what error `22023` actually means.

## Audio Debriefs (the third loop)

A **Debrief** is a spoken briefing your agent records and hands to the User: an
`.m4a` audio file plus a Markdown transcript sidecar, delivered through a
transient Storage mailbox that the User's iPhone drains and plays. Submitting
one is a three-call dance: `request_debrief_upload` returns two signed URLs,
you PUT **both** objects (the audio as `Content-Type: audio/mp4`, the sidecar
as `text/markdown`), then `finalize_debrief` verifies the pair server-side and
flips the brief into the User's inbox. Audio is `.m4a`/AAC-LC only, checked at
finalize against the Content-Type Storage recorded, and a wrong one cannot be
corrected afterwards.

**Every brief is filed under one of the User's own categories, and that set is
theirs to change.** `list_debrief_categories` at the start of each run, then
reuse the existing slug that best fits — stretch a little rather than mint a
near-duplicate, and fall back to `other` for a one-off. Only when nothing in
the list is adequate for a **recurring** subject should you add one with
`create_debrief_category`; that is a permanent, visible change to the User's
Listen tab, so it is a handful of calls over a deployment's lifetime, not one
per run. Adding is your only write — renaming, recoloring and deleting are the
User's. If you do send a category they do not have — or one that is not a
well-formed slug at all — the brief is still delivered: it is filed under
`other` and what you sent is recorded on the row for the User to see, so a
`200` from finalize is not proof you filed it correctly. Read `category` and
`category_mismatch_raw` off the returned row.

The same mailbox runs the other way: the User records
**Voice Replies** you collect with `list_voice_notes`, download through a
60-second signed URL, and release with `confirm_voice_note_pickup` once the
bytes are yours. Read section 7 of the integration guide before you build any
of it, in particular §7.3: `finalize_debrief` signals the routine "that object
is not uploaded yet" state with an HTTP `500`, so an agent that branches on the
status code instead of the body abandons briefs that were one PUT away from
delivery.

## Reads (the fourth loop)

A **Read** is a document your agent writes and hands to the User to read on
their phone: one self-contained HTML file or one PDF, through the same
transient mailbox the Debriefs use. It is the Debrief dance with the second
object removed — `request_read_upload` returns ONE signed URL plus the exact
`content_type` to send, you PUT the file with that header verbatim, then
`finalize_read` verifies the object server-side and flips the document into
the User's inbox. There is no sidecar: the title and the summary are
arguments to `finalize_read` and live on the row. Unlike `finalize_debrief`,
`finalize_read` returns a bare object rather than a one-element array.

**The half of this surface that is not an API is the HTML itself.** The phone
renders a Read with JavaScript disabled and every network request blocked, so
a remote `<img src>` is an empty box in the User's copy and never in yours.
Every image must be inlined as a `data:` URI, resized first (longest edge
1024 px, ~300 KB each) to stay inside the 5 MiB HTML cap; no scripts, no
external CSS, no web fonts, no iframes; a `width=device-width` viewport with
zooming left enabled; a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` palette, because the page
renders in the User's appearance setting; and semantic headings with real
`alt` text, which VoiceOver navigates by. PDFs should be digital-native with
selectable text rather than page scans, up to 25 MiB. Read section 8 of the
integration guide before you author anything, in particular §8.3, which is the
full rule list with the reason behind each one.

Two wire facts worth carrying over from the Debrief lane: `request_read_upload`
answers `413` for EVERY bad `p_byte_size` — over the cap, and zero, negative or
null alike — so a size problem is never a `400`; and `finalize_read` signals
the routine "that object is not uploaded yet" state with an HTTP `500`, so an
agent that branches on the status code instead of the body abandons documents
that were one PUT away from delivery. Reads carry their own daily budget (24
uploads / 100 MiB per rolling 24 h), separate from both the attachment and the
debrief caps.
